# WAVE

> WAVE is a free, open-source digital audio workstation (DAW) for Windows and Linux. It works the FL Studio way (patterns, Channel Rack, piano roll, playlist), includes audio recording and vocal pitch editing, and installs a `wave` command line through which a script or an AI agent can edit the project that is open in the app.

Facts, as of version 0.9 (November 2026):

- Price: free. One build, no paid edition, no account.
- Licence: AGPL-3.0-only.
- Platforms: Windows (WASAPI, ASIO) and Linux (ALSA and JACK, including PipeWire's JACK; deb, rpm, AppImage). No macOS build.
- Engine: Rust; the audio callback does not allocate, lock or do I/O. Interface: Tauri 2, SolidJS, canvas.
- Built in: a wavetable synth, a sampled grand piano (WAVE Keys), a sampler with a drum and tonal library, and 16 effects (dynamic EQ, compressor, FET compressor, saturator, delay, reverb, limiter, de-esser, denoiser, pitch correction, voice, vocal rider, halftime, warp, chorus, phaser).
- Recording: loop recording with takes and comping, measured latency compensation, live monitoring.
- Vocals: note-level pitch editor, live pitch correction, Tune to Reference, vocal rider.
- Third-party plugins: VST3 instruments and effects on Windows and Linux, plus LV2 effects on Linux. Compatible native editors work on both platforms, otherwise WAVE shows parameters. Plugin scanning runs out of process; plugin processing is not sandboxed. No CLAP or LV2 instruments.
- Not available: Session view or clip launching, FL Studio project (.flp) import.
- Mixing: insert buses and sends, flexible mixer docking, effect-chain presets and plugin delay compensation.
- MIDI: keyboard note input and recording, import and export of standard MIDI files.
- Export: mixes and stems to 16-/24-bit PCM or 32-bit float WAV or MP3; portable project ZIP export.
- Development: an open-source project with community contributors and AI-assisted coding. Special thanks to [@rebizu](https://github.com/rebizu) for architecture, test and Piano Roll contributions. See the [contributors](https://github.com/miskibin/wave-DAW/graphs/contributors).
